description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three measures of Accuracy: Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, with tick marks generally spaced at intervals of 0.01, though the label for 0.83 is omitted. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The "Final Accuracy" is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers and error bars. It begins at a value of approximately 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and ends at approximately 0.98 at 0.99, remaining relatively steady and high across the x-axis with a low point of approximately 0.87 at an initial confidence of 0.95. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" is shown as a dashed brown line with diamond markers and error bars. It starts at its peak of approximately 0.46 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and exhibits a general downward trend, ending at its lowest point of approximately 0.04 at 0.99, while experiencing fluctuations including notable dips to approximately 0.14 at 0.86 and 0.95. The "Initial Accuracy" is depicted by a dash-dot green line with square markers and error bars. It begins at approximately 0.54 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and shows an overall upward trend, reaching its peak of approximately 0.94 at 0.99, with intermediate fluctuations including a local peak of 0.76 at 0.86 and a dip to 0.58 at 0.88.
